title: Dhritarashtra's Anxiety
body:
Dhritarashtra's Anxiety

अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते ।
तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ।।

"There are those who always think of Me and engage in exclusive devotion to Me. To them, whose minds are always absorbed in Me, I provide what they lack and preserve what they already possess. (Gita IX-22)"

Following the miracle of the infinite robes, dark omens echoed throughout Hastinapur: jackals howled in the streets, and donkeys brayed, signaling impending cosmic retribution. Fearing these portents, Gandhari entered the scene and advised Dhritarashtra to undo his sons' misdeeds before they consumed the entire lineage. Dhritarashtra intervened, soothing Draupadi and granting her two boons. Draupadi requested the unconditional release of her husbands along with their weapons, refusing a third boon as a sign of greed.
Though the Pandavas departed for Indraprastha, Duryodhana, Sakuni, and Duhsasana upbraided the blind king for letting his prey escape on the very threshold of success. They argued that a self-respecting Kshatriya would never forgive such humiliation and that the Pandavas would return with an army to destroy them. Dhritarashtra yielded once more, sending a messenger to recall Yudhishthira for a single, final round of play. The conditions were simple: the loser would spend twelve years in forest exile (Vanavasam) and a thirteenth year incognito (Agnyatavasam); if discovered in the thirteenth year, another twelve-year cycle would begin.
Despite the warnings of his family, Yudhishthira accepted, declaring that destiny cannot be bypassed and a challenge to dice cannot be refused. He was defeated once more by Sakuni's loaded dice. As the Pandavas departed for the forest clad in deer skins, the citizens of Hastinapur openly lamented, accusing Dhritarashtra and his sons of absolute treachery. The sage Narada appeared in the court, declaring with cosmic authority: 'Fourteen years from this day, the Kauravas will become extinct as the result of the crime committed by Duryodhana.'
